_readme: The data flow on the How it works page (UI_SPEC.md section 13). Edit the words freely; names use the tour's kinds and api/tests/test_tour_lineage.py checks every one against the code.

steps.text: Every hour, Airflow lists new activities, then reads each one's detail (the list has no description). It picks up from a watermark and stays under Strava's rate limit.
Each activity lands as Strava sent it, minus the GPS fields.
SQL loads it into the star schema with idempotent upserts.
Hevy writes lifting sessions into the description as text; a parser turns it into one row per set. Lines it can't read go to quarantine with a reason.
An iPhone Shortcut posts yesterday's and today's samples with a bearer token.
The batch is stored as received; one sent twice is recognised by its SHA-256 and skipped.
Each sample is checked, then becomes a fact; a bad one is quarantined.
Targets, the weight goal, the weekend rule and recovery days. A target applies from the day it is set, so past days keep theirs.
The business rules are SQL functions, worked out when a page asks: what kind of day each day was, the streak (window functions over gaps and islands), and nutrition against the target.
FastAPI serves them as JSON to this React app.
Every run is a row with its status and counts. Every hour, 15 data-quality checks run, each a plain SQL file, and the Me page shows the results.
